s: Record dispatches put the spotlight on margins
Maruti sold 696,654 vehicles in the September quarter, up 26.5%
year on year. Yet it earned less operating profit on each vehicle.
Using company-reported EBIT and total dispatches, operating profit
per vehicle fell from roughly INR 61,400 to INR 40,200. This
measure includes the wider business, but it captures why volume
growth alone gives an incomplete picture.
The company attributed the operating squeeze to commodity
inflation. Losses on the invested surplus then deepened the decline in
net profit. The distinction matters for forecasts. A reversal in
investment marks can lift earnings in a single quarter, while restoring
vehicle profitability requires better pricing, mix or costs.
Demand offers some protection. At September-end Maruti reported
about 200,000 pending bookings and 17 days of dealer inventory.
October dispatches reached 276,120 units, including 49,872 exports.
The order book supports production, although bookings can cancel
and dispatches can run ahead of retail sales.
Our November 2027 target of INR 12,300 implies 5.4% price upside.
It assumes FY28 operating margin recovers to 7.3% and investors
pay 25 times those earnings. The next two quarterly results should
show whether stronger volumes are finally translating into profit.

H1 consolidated revenue was approximately INR 105,826 crore. Our INR 215,000 crore FY27 forecast therefore needs
INR 109,174 crore in H2, about 6.6% above the prior H2. October volumes support that step-up, but the September order
backlog cannot establish the price or mix of the cars ultimately delivered.
We assume FY27/FY28/FY29 EBITDA margins of 9.8%, 10.9% and 11.5%, versus 11.7% in FY26. Annual
depreciation is 3.6% of revenue. The FY28 case needs only a partial recovery from the H1 cost shock, but even that
requires commodity inflation to moderate or pricing to catch up. FY28 and FY29 consolidated revenue grows 9% and
Add combined non-operating and associate income of INR 3,400 / 3,800 / 4,000 crore in FY27-29 and deduct interest of
INR 260 / 280 / 300 crore. Apply a 25% effective tax rate and assume zero minority allocation and constant 31.44 crore
shares. This yields FY28 parent EPS of INR 492.07.
The reference price implies 23.7x FY28 EPS. At a 25x multiple, it requires EPS of INR 466.88. We select 25x as a
modest premium to the implied forward multiple for Maruti’s scale and backlog, tempered by margin cyclicality. It is a
judgement, close to the 25.0x paid on FY26 actual EPS at the reference price. Cash is already represented through

A 100 bp change in FY28 operating margin changes after-tax EPS by INR 55.90, or roughly INR 1398 per share at 25x.
This is the largest operating swing in the target. Watch reported EBIT alongside average selling price and discounts.
Q2 SUV sales rose 68.2% and domestic market share reached 40.8%. Exports slipped to 108,119 vehicles from 110,487.
The bull case needs higher-margin mix and sustained domestic retail demand as capacity ramps. Lower bookings, rising
dealer stock and heavier incentives would weaken it.
FY26 operating cash flow of about INR 19,100 crore exceeded estimated capital expenditure of INR 10,346 crore,
leaving INR 8,754 crore before financing. Capacity additions and EV investment could absorb that cushion. This simple
cash measure differs from unlevered free cash flow.
At INR 11,672, an Overweight view requires fair value above INR 13,423, or FY28 EPS above INR 537 at 25x.
Underweight begins below INR 10,505, equivalent to EPS below INR 420. Sustained EBIT-margin recovery or renewed
compression matters more than a single strong dispatch month.
First coverage. One price observation precedes initiation.
